$comment: Lint baseline (PHASE-0 T3). Every count below may only FALL: check-lint-baseline.mjs fails the build when any rule or diagnostic code exceeds its pin, when an unpinned rule reports findings, or when either total rises. Counts are PER RULE, not just totals, so a rise in one rule cannot hide behind a fall in another. Seeded 2026-07-27 at commit fc662b6 from the commands recorded in each section, run on a clean, instrument-free tree. The eslint rules are all severity `warn` in eslint.config.js on purpose — the tree has hundreds of pre-existing findings and error-mode would be unshippable; this file is the enforcement, not the severity. To LOWER entries after real fixes: node deploy/checks/check-lint-baseline.mjs --tighten. To RAISE one, or to admit a newly enabled rule, edit this file BY HAND in a gate-side-only commit — that edit is meant to be seen and reviewed. No tool raises a number.

eslint.$comment: Findings by rule id. `--no-inline-config` is part of the command and is not optional: without it a one-line eslint-disable comment lowers the count without fixing anything. no-constant-binary-expression is pinned at 0 — the rule IS enabled and the tree is genuinely clean of it, so any future finding is a rise from zero.

Command: `npx eslint packages/server/src --no-inline-config -f json`, then group the no-restricted-imports messages by file:line. THE ANSWER IS THREE CLASSES, NOT TWO, and the third is the reason the flip is impossible honestly. (1) AGENT-NAMED — 37 sites. The fs/proc call acts on a resource the AGENT CHOOSES: a path, a command, a URL out of tool arguments. THIS SET IS THE REQUIREMENT (*nothing an agent can reach touches fs/proc/net except through a broker*). Sites: agent/canvas-view.ts:19 · agent/image-prep.ts:31,32 · agent/path-resolve.ts:16 · agent/pdf-tools.ts:23 · agent/runtime.ts:5 · agent/system-control.ts:19,20 · agent/tools/cat/canvas.ts:23 · agent/tools/cat/comms.ts:47 · agent/tools/cat/fs.ts:35 · agent/tools/cat/media.ts:41 · agent/tools/process-run.ts:19 · agent/tools/util.ts:19 · google/tools-slides.ts:11 · memory/large-files.ts:1 · microsoft/tools-office.ts:6 · plaud/client.ts:14 · services/audio-generation.ts:27 · services/canvas-html.ts:18 · services/email-attachments.ts:10 · services/generation-jobs.ts:28 · services/image-generation.ts:25 · services/imessage-bridge.ts:5,6 · services/office-render.ts:16 · services/public-share.ts:16 · services/transcription.ts:18,21 · services/video-generation.ts:21 · services/video-job-poller.ts:24 · techniques/dependencies.ts:36 · techniques/share-import.ts:10 · techniques/store.ts:5 · techniques/tools.ts:5 · techniques/versioning.ts:5 · tools/index-generator.ts:7. (2) AGENT-TRIGGERED, PLATFORM-NAMED — 17 sites. A tool call can make the code run, but every path and command is a platform literal the agent cannot influence (self-update, the watchdog bundle, voice model files, the tunnel pidfile, the PM/Dreamer soul templates). Routing these through agent-facing brokers is exactly what P5-R12 forbids: it would record an agent-facing fs site that does not exist and make the count LIE. Sites: gateway/routes/update.ts:6,8 · services/resource-monitor.ts:6 · services/tunnel.ts:6,7 · services/watchdog-refresh.ts:25,27 · tracker/pm-agent.ts:1 · update-state.ts:18 · update/artifact-integrity.ts:48 · vault/maintenance.ts:8 · voice/custom-voices.ts:25 · voice/model-manager.ts:1,2 · voice/stt-service.ts:1,2 · voice/tts-service.ts:4. (3) PLATFORM-INTERNAL — 41 sites. No tool path at all: boot, the database, migration import/export, logging, the dashboard's own HTTP routes, dependency installers. Sites: agent/v2/receipt.ts:23 · config/loader.ts:1 · db/connection.ts:2 · db/migrations.ts:1 · gateway/routes/agents.ts:3 · gateway/routes/config.ts:4 · gateway/routes/migration.ts:6,11 · gateway/routes/services.ts:8 · gateway/routes/setup-deps.ts:7,8 · gateway/routes/techniques.ts:6 · gateway/routes/upload.ts:3 · gateway/server.ts:6 · healer/healer-agent.ts:13 · imaginer/imaginer-agent.ts:24 · index.ts:2 · logger.ts:1 · memory/assembly-validation-sink.ts:54 · microsoft/office-packages.ts:6 · migration/checks.ts:5,8 · migration/export.ts:5 · migration/fs-copy.ts:5 · migration/import.ts:5 · migration/manifest.ts:6 · migration/path-migration.ts:5 · migration/step-classify.ts:16,19 · plaud/auth.ts:10 · prompt/assembler.ts:1 · providers/anthropic-sdk-auth.ts:5 · screen-share/manager.ts:17 · services/ensure-system-deps.ts:20,22 · techniques/share-export.ts:12 · techniques/trainer-agent.ts:1 · twilio/sms-inbound.ts:8 · voice/smart-turn.ts:29,30 · voice/voice-assets.ts:8. WHY THE FLIP DOES NOT LAND HERE, said plainly: the brokers AUTHORIZE a declared effect at the executor's gate loop, before dispatch — they do not perform the I/O. So a handler that has been authorized still has to call `fs`, and the rule counts that call's import. Satisfying the rule over class (1) needs an fs/proc FACADE that performs the I/O behind the brokers, and no plan in this folder builds one. Inventing it inside a phase-exit task would be a large refactor of 37 sites with no capability gained and the exit battery still to run. TRANSFERRED, per P5-R12 step 3, to SWEEP-G (the last sweep, and the only point at which class (1) stops moving — every earlier sweep relocates some of these files), with the precondition stated: the flip requires the facade decision first, and if that decision is NOT taken the honest outcome is to retire the "flips ENFORCED" wording rather than leave a gate nobody can pass. THE DIRECTION IS STILL ENFORCED MEANWHILE, which is what actually protects the surface: this baseline may only FALL, and every raise is a reviewed by-hand gate-side edit that has to name the alternatives it measured and refused — the three $raise entries below are that record.

(a) `fs/promises.readFile` is the same restricted family AND would hold a tens-of-megabyte platform zip in memory to hash it — a worse answer that does not even move the count. (b) Routing it through a broker is the wrong shape and would make the count lie: the brokers exist to put an AGENT'S declared effects behind a gate, and this path is platform-internal update machinery no agent can reach, so a broker call here would record an agent-facing fs site that does not exist. The rule is advisory by its own message and exists to MEASURE the surface Phase 5's brokers must route; this is that surface growing by one, named, with its file and its job, so T7 re-derives a count it can trust rather than one that was gamed. Verifying downloaded bytes before overwriting a working install is the task.

THE RULE COUNTS IMPORT STATEMENTS, AND A SPLIT MULTIPLIES THEM WITHOUT ADDING ONE BYTE OF NEW fs ACCESS. `agent/tools.ts` held ONE `node:fs` import serving every fs-touching handler in a 268-case switch. T4 moves those handlers into per-category modules, and a module that calls `fs.statSync` must import `node:fs` itself — so the SAME calls, byte for byte, now need one import statement per module instead of one for the file. AMENDED 2026-08-02, same task, same mechanism, +1 more (92 -> 93) for `agent/tools/cat/media.ts`, whose four generators write the produced asset into the calling agent's uploads dir, and +1 more again (93 -> 94) for `agent/tools/cat/canvas.ts`, whose `canvas_render` stats the file it is asked to put on the canvas. This raise is +2 for the comms category: `agent/tools/cat/comms.ts` (share_file / show_to_user / share_publicly read and stat the paths they publish) and `agent/tools/util.ts` (registerSharedFile, which every category that mints a download URL calls, and which therefore may not live in any one category module). Both were merged to a SINGLE statement each rather than left as the two the conversion produced (`import fs, { existsSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'`). The alternative that would hold the count flat is a shared fs facade invented during a relocation, which is exactly the improvement-during-a-move this task forbids; the honest answer is that the count is a proxy for direct fs access and the access did not change. T7 re-derives this number when the split is finished and `agent/tools.ts` is gone. NOT a licence for new fs sites: any raise that is not a relocation still owes its own reason.

This raise is the transitional state between 'the brokers decide and nothing carries' and 'nothing an agent can reach touches fs/proc except through the facade'. THE DIRECTION IS STILL ENFORCED: every other rule is unchanged and this one may not rise again without another hand edit.

unusedSymbols.$comment: Findings by TypeScript diagnostic code, from tsconfig.lint.json (noUnusedLocals + noUnusedParameters). That config is consumed ONLY by `npm run lint:types` — never by the build and never by `npm run typecheck` — so the unused-symbol population is counted without breaking either. TS6133 = declared but never read; TS6192 = all imports in a declaration unused; TS6196 = declared but never used (type position). 116 of the 118 sit in packages/server; the other 2 are in packages/shared, which the server program pulls in through its project reference.
